title: /backlog per-project "Up next" lists tasks in tree order, not ranked like Home's Up next
description:
## Problem

Each project section on `/workspace/:urlKey/backlog` has its own "Up next" list (3 per project, `UP_NEXT_PER_PROJECT` in `lib/home-view.js`, split by `splitProjectRoots`, also paged by the `up-next` kind of `/api/home-rows` via `homeRowsFor` in `lib/home-rows.js`). It takes a project's open unstarted root tasks in **project tree order** (the order `buildForest` leaves them in), so it has the same defect that Home's "Up next" had until LIN-4139: it is not a priority order. A project's older, lower-priority Todo tasks can sit in its "Up next" while higher-priority ready tasks are folded behind "show more".

## Why it matters

Home's Up next was ranked in LIN-4139 (ready tasks, then priority, due date, newest, one per epic, with a one-line reason). The `/backlog` page uses the same words "Up next" for a different, unranked list, so the two disagree about what is next, and the operator's complaint ("they're certainly not 'Up next'") applies there too. Impact is limited to a secondary page, hence Low.

## Acceptance

* Decide first whether the per-project list should be ranked like Home's (same rule: ready only, priority, due date, newest created, tree position) or renamed so it no longer claims to be "Up next". Record the choice and the reason.
* If ranked: a project's `/backlog` "Up next" shows its highest-ranked ready unstarted tasks; a lower-priority task never ranks above a ready higher-priority one in the same project; the "show more" fold and `/api/home-rows` (`kind: up-next`) page the same order, so a task is shown once.
* Home's Up next and the `/backlog` lists do not repeat a task that Home already shows (existing behaviour, keep it).
* No existing test's assertions are weakened; update `public/llms.txt` if `render.js` DOM changes.

## Anchors

* `lib/home-view.js`: `UP_NEXT_PER_PROJECT` (\~:26), `splitProjectRoots` (\~:241), its call in `buildHomeView` (\~:518); `upNextOf` is the ranking to reuse or share.
* `lib/home-rows.js`: `homeRowsFor` (\~:143-159), the `upNextRest` / `backlog` kinds.
* Tests that pin the order: `tests/unit/lin-4113-home-desk.test.js`, `tests/unit/lin-4024-home-rows.test.js`.

## Unvalidated idea

Factor the ranking comparator out of `upNextOf` and sort each project's unstarted roots with it before the `UP_NEXT_PER_PROJECT` split. Unchecked: whether per-project "one per epic" makes sense, and how it interacts with the fold's paging.

## Provenance

Found in review of LIN-4139 (PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2250](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2250>), merged as 26a33145), classed outside that ticket because the plan left `/backlog` alone. Priority: Low, because it affects only the secondary backlog page and no data or action. Type: Improvement (the workspace label catalog's closest type label for a behaviour gap in an existing feature).

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Two Surveys at LinearViewer `172f644a1` (on LIN-4150) agree:

* **Readiness has no input where the split happens.** `splitProjectRoots` sees only the tree; readiness in `upNextOf` comes from `buildBlockingGraph(orderedCards)`. And it has **two callers that each split for themselves:** `buildHomeView` (the first three) and `homeRowsFor` (which rebuilds the view and splits again to page the fold). Give each its own sort and page and fold disagree, so a task is shown twice or not at all.
* **"Ready only" must sort, not filter.** This list plus its fold is the only place a project's Todo roots appear on `/backlog`. Dropping blocked roots breaks `lin-4117-reachability-property`. Rank ready roots first, then blocked ones, by the same keys.
* **"One per epic" means nothing here:** each row is a root with its subtree. Leave the cap out.
* **Custom-state roots** count toward the three and always stay visible today. Keep that, and say so.
* **The tests won't notice either way:** the pinned fixtures (`lin-4024-home-view`, `lin-4024-home-rows`) have equal priority and no dates, so every key ties. The task needs its own witness.
* **The page never shows the words "Up next"** (its fold reads "show N more"). The name lives only in identifiers, the module header and `llms.txt`. So the real decision is the order.
* **The acceptance is wrong about dedupe:** the project list dedupes only against Running and Waiting, not Home's Up next. A task can sit in both today, and ranking will put Home's top tasks at the head of their project lists. Keep that; an exclusion would change what can be reached.

### Scope decision (5 Nov, about 03:10 UTC)

John asked Claude to take the human's role in this process and to err on the side of larger tidies. **The choice is to rank, not rename** (the name was never on the page; the order is what's wrong). **The decision: one ranking, and one derivation of the project split for page and fold.** In pieces:

1. **Rank, through one exported ranking.**
   * First a failing witness: a project with a Low Todo root first and a High Todo root fourth; assert High is in the first three and the `up-next` fold doesn't return it. Run `lin-4117-reachability-property` beside it.
   * Then export one ranking (the keys and the comparator) out of `upNextOf`, used by `upNextOf` and the split, with no copy of `compareKeys`/`timeOr`/the keys. Ready roots first, then blocked, no epic cap, custom-state roots kept visible.
   * **One derivation:** `buildHomeView` returns each project's ranked rest, and `homeRowsFor` pages that instead of re-splitting.
   * Update the module header and `llms.txt` (:72, :123) to say what the list is and how it's ordered.
2. **Names that now describe** `/backlog` (its own piece, after 1): `upNext`/`UP_NEXT_PER_PROJECT`, the "Home's folds" comments in `render.js`, and `kind: 'up-next'` if it can be renamed without breaking a caller (keep the old kind accepted if anything outside the page uses it). If this touches more than identifiers and comments, stop and say so.

**At merge (we'll check it):**

* a higher-priority ready root never ranks below a lower one in the same project, on the page or in the fold;
* one ranking function, used by Home's Up next and `/backlog`; no second comparator;
* page and fold come from one derivation; the reachability property still holds;
* **who else must learn about it:** the module header, `llms.txt`, and any comment that calls the list "Home's".

**Not this task's** (the place view said so; they go to the tally): separating `upNextOf`'s eligibility from its ranking; splitting the 576-line `home-view.js`.

## Implementation Plan

fits one session
plan-review due: no

**Implemented as approved** in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2283](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2283>) (merged as `13fe24a0`, deployed). The plan's pieces landed: one exported ranking (`rankKeysOf`, `compareRank`, `blockedIdsOf`) used by `upNextOf` and the project split; `buildHomeView` returns `projectSplits` and `homeRowsFor` pages it without re-splitting; names and docs updated (`PROJECT_LEAD_ROOTS`, split fields `lead`/`leadRest`, module headers, `render.js` comment, `source-map.md`, `llms.txt` :72/:123). Deviations: `projectSplits` is a `Map`, not a plain object (never serialised). Two plan items review found missing were finished at close-out: the `lin-4117-reachability-property` case with a blocked High root, and the `lead`/`leadRest` field rename. The full plan, with its witnesses and risk list, is preserved in the task snapshots (captured 2026-11-05T03:45Z) and the comment trail.

comments.body: Label note: the workspace label catalog has a fitting type label (`Improvement`), but the proxy offers no label write (PATCH accepts no label field), so no label could be set. Please add `Improvement` by hand. Priority is set (Low) with its reason in the description.

Drift & Coherence Review 2026-11-03 (LIN-4153, report PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2253). Delta comment, not a body edit.

Per-project Up next and the deck's top task still rank differently: `splitProjectRoots` (`home-view.js:241-256`) takes the first three Todo tasks in tree order; `upNextOf` (`home-view.js:412`) ranks by priority and due date; the deck top task (`home-pipeline.js:67-68`) uses `orderIssuesForSwipe`. Readiness counts in-deck blockers only (`home-view.js:414-416`). Triage is split out to LIN-4158.

LIN-4151 implementation is up as PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2283 (branch feat/lin-4151-backlog-lead-ranking, commits 10f4fd07 and d3dc86df).

What changed: /backlog's per-project lead list is ranked by the same comparator as Home's Up next (ready before blocked, then priority, due date, newest created, tree position). The three shown roots and the "show N more" fold page one ranked sequence, computed once in buildHomeView (projectSplits); homeRowsFor pages it and no longer re-splits. Readiness sorts and never filters, so blocked roots stay reachable. Dedupe is unchanged. Decision: rank, not rename (the page never says "Up next").

Evidence: five new witnesses in tests/unit/lin-4151-project-lead-ranking.test.js failed on the unchanged code and pass now; the all-keys-tie guard passes throughout. npm run test:unit: 23209 pass, 0 fail. Playwright on the related home/backlog specs: 40 pass. CI on the PR: all checks green (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan).

## Review — LIN-4151

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2283 at head `d3dc86df` (commits 10f4fd07 + d3dc86df on base 172f644a).

CI: green on d3dc86df. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all passed (run 41960255661).

**Scope vs plan.** The diff covers the plan's places: `lib/home-view.js`, `lib/home-rows.js`, `lib/render.js` (comment only), `public/llms.txt` :72/:123, `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, one test import, and the new witness file. Nothing overran the plan. There are no DOM or wire changes: `kind=up-next`, `upNextMore`, `home-fold-up-next` and `data-home-fetch` are unchanged. Deviations:
- `projectSplits` is a `Map` rather than a plain object. Harmless: `homeView` is never serialised whole (`homeRowDataFor` reads `trees`, `inProgressTrees`, `recent.nodes` and `upNext` only).
- Two plan items are missing. Both are in the ledger below.

**Checked against the at-merge conditions**
- A higher-priority ready root never ranks below a lower one, on the page or in the fold. Yes: the split sorts with `compareRank` before the cut (W1, W3).
- One ranking. `rankKeysOf` and `compareRank` are exported and used by both `upNextOf` and `splitProjectRoots`. The old inline key chain in `upNextOf` is gone and no copy remains. `blockedIdsOf` mirrors `upNextOf`'s old card choice exactly: seeds are skipped, the first card per identifier decides, and the lookup is `key || id`. `upNextOf` still *filters* blocked tasks, so Home's eligibility is unchanged.
- One derivation. `homeRowsFor` pages `view.projectSplits.get(projectId)`, and `splitProjectRoots` is no longer exported. The page (`gatherHomePage`) and the fold (`server.js:3713`) build the view from the same gathered inputs, including `orderedCards` and `rulingRows`. Positions come from `indexNodes`, which walks the project trees first, so ties fall back to tree order.
- Dedupe is unchanged: the split still takes `shown` and `waiting`.

**Regression check.** I ran `git log` on the touched files (LIN-4243, 4242, 4145, 4139, 4120, 4119, 4117). The `waiting` argument added by LIN-4242/4243 still reaches the split. LIN-4145's `fullById` and parent link are untouched. LIN-4139's `upNextOf` behaviour is identical. Nothing reverted is re-applied. Since the ticket was created, nothing has changed on `main` in `home-view.js` or `home-rows.js` other than this PR, so the anchors hold.

**Tests, re-run by me**
- The 11 related unit files (lin-4151, 4117-*, 4024-home-*, 4113-home-desk, 4139-*, 4119-*, 4120-*) pass on the head: 161/161.
- I ran the new witness file against base 172f644a: W1–W5 fail and the W6 guard passes, matching the implementation report.
- Mutations (each reverted afterwards):
  - M1 removed the sort from the split: W1–W5 go red.
  - M2 dropped the `blocked` key from `compareRank`: W2 and W3 go red.
  - M3 looked readiness up by `id` only instead of `key || id`: W2 and W3 go red.
  - M5 filtered blocked roots out instead of sorting them: W2 and W3 go red, **but `lin-4117-reachability-property` stays green**. See ledger item 1.
  - M6 made the fold page a different order from the page: W3, W4 and `lin-4024-home-rows` go red.
  - M4 dropped the position tie-break: only `lin-4139` goes red, not W6, because the stable sort already preserves tree order. Not a defect, since the key is still pinned by lin-4139.

**Isolated, or one of a class?** The class is "a lead list cut in tree order instead of by the shared ranking". Its instances are Home's Up next (already ranked in LIN-4139), the project lead list (fixed here) and the project's Backlog fold. The Backlog fold stays in tree order **outside** the class: the plan excluded it with a reason, since Backlog and triage roots make no "next" claim. The deck top task (`orderIssuesForSwipe`) and in-deck-only readiness are **outside**; they belong to the Drift review's findings, triaged to LIN-4158. Nothing else needs filing.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **Inside** (the plan's witness list and the at-merge condition "the reachability property still holds", class: blocked roots stay reachable). The reachability property never runs with the ranking doing real work. Its scenarios carry no priorities or `blocksIds`, and `placementsOf` calls `homeRowsFor` without `orderedCards`. As a result, mutation M5 (filtering blocked roots out of the split) leaves it green. The plan required this extension and it is missing. **Settle before the merge:** close-out adds the case to `tests/unit/lin-4117-reachability-property.test.js`:
   - Thread `orderedCards` through `scenario` and `placementsOf`, so `homeRowsFor` gets the same cards as `buildHomeView`.
   - Add a scenario of ≥5 unstarted roots with mixed `priority`, where one High root is blocked by an open card (`blocksIds` naming its `key`).
   - Assert `assertPlacedOnce`.
   - Distinguishing check: with M5 applied (`.filter(root => !blocked.has(root.issue.identifier))` after the `!isBacklog` filter in `splitProjectRoots`) the new case goes red; reverted, it is green. The added case must not weaken any existing assertion.
2. **Inside** (scope decision part 2, "Names that now describe `/backlog`"). Only the constant was renamed (`PROJECT_LEAD_ROOTS`). The split's result fields are still `upNext`/`upNextRest`, and since `projectSplits` exposes them they now leak beyond the module. **Settle before the merge (identifiers only):**
   - In `lib/home-view.js`, rename the split's return fields to `lead`/`leadRest`: in `splitProjectRoots`, its JSDoc, the destructure in `buildHomeView`'s `homeTrees` map, and the `projectSplits` `@returns` type.
   - In `lib/home-rows.js:159`, change `split.upNextRest` to `split.leadRest`.
   - Leave the render prop `upNextMore`, `kind: 'up-next'` and every DOM name unchanged.
   - The distinguishing check is that the unit suite stays green and `grep -n "upNextRest" lib` returns nothing.
   - If close-out judges this not worth the churn, the alternative is to drop it with that reason. Filing a ticket does not discharge it.
3. **Outside, nothing to settle:** no browser test drives `/backlog` with mixed priorities. The order is computed entirely server-side, in the same `buildHomeView`/`homeRowsFor` functions the witnesses call. The server wiring (`server.js:3713` and `gatherHomePage`) is unchanged and I read it, and there are no DOM changes. CI covers this deliverable apart from items 1 and 2.

No DECISION is raised; none is needed.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The fix is correct, one ranking and one derivation as decided, and mutation-proven. Close-out should add the missing reachability-property case (item 1) and either finish or explicitly drop the field rename (item 2), then re-check CI on the new head.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** It mostly wasn't; the plan was precise and its anchors still matched HEAD. Where it bound was `buildHomeView`'s ordering: the split ran before `indexNodes`, so positions didn't exist yet, and readiness lived inside `upNextOf`. Moving `indexNodes` up and lifting readiness out (`blockedIdsOf`) was the real work. The rest was being careful: one function of ~600 lines where every addition is order-sensitive, and the `key || id` vs identifier lookup that would silently rank blocked roots as ready.

**2. What would I have done first?** Land the extraction (`blockedIdsOf`, `rankKeysOf`/`compareRank`, `upNextOf` using them) as a no-behaviour-change commit with Home's tests green, then change the split. I did both in one commit, so the refactor and the behaviour change can't be reviewed apart.

**3. What would I tidy?** Two plan items I didn't finish, and should have said so plainly in the PR: the split's result fields are still `upNext`/`upNextRest` (I renamed only the constant), and I covered reachability in the new file rather than extending `lin-4117-reachability-property`. Also, `compareRank` carries a `blocked` key that is always false inside `upNextOf`, because Up next still filters. It's harmless, but it reads oddly until eligibility and ranking are separated. The three new exports are only tested through `buildHomeView`.

**4. What would this ticket have been?** If ranking were its own module, separate from Home's placement, the ticket would be "pass each project's roots through the ranking": one call and one test. Most of this diff was building that seam inside `home-view.js`.

**5. What did the ticket get wrong?** The original acceptance asked for "ready only" (which breaks reachability) and dedupe against Home's Up next (not today's behaviour). The Survey caught both. The plan specified `projectSplits` as a plain object, but it's indexed by a query-string `projectId`, so `?project=constructor` would hit the prototype. I used a `Map`. Otherwise the plan held, including its claim that `positionOf` reproduces tree order on ties.

**6. What did it leave behind?** Simpler: readiness is read once per view, and `homeRowsFor` no longer derives anything for projects. A fold can't disagree with its page by construction. Still in two places: `orderIssuesForSwipe` remains a second "what's next" ordering beside `compareRank`, so the drift review's three rankers are now two, not one. New without a home: `projectSplits` is a view field only the fold reads. Stale: the wire and DOM names (`kind: 'up-next'`, `upNextMore`, `home-fold-up-next`) now name a list that isn't Up next, explained only by comments, and `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-03.md` still lists `splitProjectRoots` as a ranker (a historical record, so I left it).

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** The one-derivation part paid for itself outright. Sorting in only one caller would have produced exactly the shown-twice or never-shown bug the Survey predicted, and it was cheap because the view already held everything. The shared comparator was small and paid too. The naming piece was the marginal part. It cost reading time across `render.js`, `llms.txt` and `source-map.md`, and I only half-did the identifiers, which tells you where the value ran out. I'd draw the line at rank, one derivation, and docs. I'd leave the identifier renames for when `home-view.js` is split, because renaming `upNext` inside the same file as Home's own `upNext` risks confusing the two more than it clarifies.

## Close-out — LIN-4151

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2283, squash-merged as `13fe24a0`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 05fc23a7`. `/backlog`'s per-project lead roots are now ranked by the one shared comparator (ready before blocked, priority, due, newest, tree position). The page's three and the "show N more" fold come from one derivation (`projectSplits`). Rank, not rename.

**Review verdict:** Approve, conditional on the ledger (review comment of 5 Nov 03:26). Both inside items were settled before the merge.

### Changes I made after the approval
| Commit | Review line it answers | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `05fc23a7` | Ledger 1: reachability property never ran with the ranking at work | `tests/unit/lin-4117-reachability-property.test.js`: `orderedCards` threaded through `scenario` and `placementsOf` (and the fold calls), plus a new case: 7 unstarted roots with mixed priorities and a High root blocked by an open card (`key`/`blocksIds`). It asserts `assertPlacedOnce`, the page's three are `U-6, M-3, L-1`, and the blocked High root is last in the fold. No existing assertion changed. |
| `05fc23a7` | Ledger 2: split fields still `upNext`/`upNextRest` | `lib/home-view.js`, `lib/home-rows.js`: the split returns `lead`/`leadRest` (function, JSDoc, `buildHomeView` destructure, `projectSplits` type, `home-rows.js` read). Identifiers only: `upNextMore`, `kind: 'up-next'`, `home-fold-up-next`, `data-home-fetch` untouched. |

### Ledger
1. **Inside, reachability case: settled.** Distinguishing check run: with review's mutation M5 applied (`.filter(root => !blocked.has(root.issue.identifier))` after the `!isBacklog` filter), the new case goes red (15 pass / 1 fail); reverted, 16/16 green. Before this, M5 left the file green.
2. **Inside, field rename: settled** (done, not dropped). `grep -rn upNextRest lib` returns nothing; `npm run test:unit` 23210 pass, 0 fail.
3. **Outside, no browser test drives `/backlog` with mixed priorities:** review classed it as nothing to settle (order is computed server-side in the functions the witnesses call; no DOM or wire change). No follow-up filed.

### CI
CI exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). On the exact merged head `05fc23a7` (run 41961939944): Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, CI success all pass. Re-read immediately before the merge: head unchanged, mergeable.

### After the deploy
Deploy landed: https://harbour.cat footer reports `13fe24a04acb…` (was `172f644a` before). On what landed, the public `llms.txt` now carries the LIN-4151 ordering text at :72 and :123.
**Not run:** an authenticated look at production `/backlog` with a mixed-priority project. This session has no signed-in session on harbour.cat. Anyone with a workspace login can run it: open `/workspace/<urlKey>/backlog`, and in a project whose first three Todo roots are lower priority than a later one, confirm the High ready root is among the three shown and the "show N more" fold continues in order. The ranking itself is proven at the merged head by the CI witnesses (W1-W6, the extended reachability property) and review's mutations M1-M3, M5, M6. No monitor is named by review, and none is claimed.

### Follow-ups and related tickets
- No outside items to file: review found none. The deck top task (`orderIssuesForSwipe`) and in-deck-only readiness were already triaged to LIN-4158.
- Related LIN-4139 is already Done; nothing to close or cancel.
- Label: `Improvement` could not be set (the proxy has no label write, per the earlier note on this ticket); please add it by hand.

### Description
Pre-prune snapshot confirmed (`GET /issues/LIN-4151/snapshots`: captured 2026-11-05T03:45Z, 17048 chars, includes the plan). The Implementation Plan body is replaced with a stub (heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no` kept word for word; links the PR; "implemented as approved", with the one deviation, `projectSplits` as a `Map`). Problem, acceptance, anchors, provenance and the scope decision are kept.
